description: Hi, I’m a Computer Engineering student interested in software development, data analysis, AI/ML, and building interactive projects. For NASA Space Apps 2026, I’ll be taking on the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge as a solo participant.
summary:
Humanity’s return to Mars requires safe, autonomous surface traversal planning across hazardous extraterrestrial topography. Astro-nah is a real-time Martian Surface Navigation and Extravehicular Activity (EVA) Traversal Engine engineered for Jezero Crater.

Integrating 20-meter NASA MRO CTX Digital Elevation Models, sub-meter HiRISE imagery, and USGS geologic maps, Astro-nah solves planetary pathfinding where standard engines fail. Planetary rovers and astronauts face steep crater scarps and wheel rollover risks. Astro-nah introduces a cost-weighted, physics-informed A* routing algorithm that penalizes dangerous slopes, cumulative ascent, and regolith traction loss under Mars’s 0.38g gravity.

Key innovations include an interactive Ancient Lake Jezero paleolake simulator (testing route submersion and shoreline avoidance at the canonical -2,395m delta highstand), a 38-second 1-Click Automated Mission Briefing for evaluators, real-time EVA telemetry with a Local Mean Solar Time sunset deadline, interactive 3D WebGL terrain orbits, and an exportable Mission Dossier with a scan-to-mobile QR code. Astro-nah bridges orbital satellite cartography and ground navigation for safe Martian exploration.
details:
WHAT DOES IT DO & HOW DOES IT WORK?

Astro-nah is an autonomous surface traversal engine designed for Martian mission operations in Jezero Crater. Users can place arbitrary Origin and Destination waypoints across the Jezero delta or select authentic Perseverance rover milestones (such as the Octavia E. Butler Landing Site to Kodiak Butte).

The platform utilizes a cost-weighted A* algorithm implemented in Python/NumPy on a 20-meter resolution Digital Terrain Model (DTM). The cost function penalizes slopes exceeding vehicle thresholds:

- Rover Mode: Hard safety ceiling of 15° with 0.12 km/h traversal speed.

- Astronaut EVA Mode: Human capability ceiling of 25° with 1.1 km/h walking speed and metabolic/oxygen consumption modeling.

In addition to safe trajectory calculation, Astro-nah features:

1. Ancient Lake Jezero Paleolake Flooding Simulator (~3.7 Ga): Users can flood the crater DEM to simulate the ancient lake. At the published delta-forming highstand (-2,395 m; Fassett & Head 2005; Mangold et al. 2021 Science), the tool calculates route submersion percentage, maximum water depth, and provides a 1-click option to reroute along the dry delta shoreline.

2. 1-Click Automated Mission Briefing ("Play Demo"): A 38-second automated tour that walks judges through target acquisition, 3-tier slope hazard scanning, A* route computation, paleolake flooding, live EVA telemetry, and mission dossier generation.

3. 3D WebGL Crater Orbit: High-performance 3D visualization with interactive sunlight positioning, vertical relief exaggeration, sub-meter HiRISE lens inspection, and a physical 3D paleowater plane.

4. Mission Dossier & Mobile QR Dispatch: Generates a comprehensive flight plan with an instant scan-to-mobile QR code that loads the exact route on any smartphone without login or registration.

WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE & WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT?

Terrestrial routing tools assume paved roads and flat horizons. On Mars, path planning requires continuous slope gradient analysis, energetic climb budgeting, and impassable cliff avoidance. Astro-nah demonstrates that naive Euclidean shortest paths intersect hazardous >20° scarps, whereas our algorithm discovers natural depositional saddles.

The intended impact is providing astronauts, autonomous rovers, and planetary researchers with instant, high-fidelity traversal feasibility assessments without requiring heavy GIS desktop software.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE & SOFTWARE USED:

- Frontend: React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet / React-Leaflet, Three.js / WebGL, Lucide Icons, Canvas API.

- Backend & Algorithms: Python 3.11, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, Rasterio, GDAL.

- Planetary Cartography & Data Processing: NASA Mars Trek REST API, USGS Astrogeology ISIS3, QGIS, MRO CTX DTM (20m/px), MRO HiRISE (25cm/px GeoTIFF), USGS SIM 3464 Shapefiles/GeoJSON.

- Deployment & CI/CD: Vercel (Production Frontend), GitHub (Version Control & Documentation).

HOW IS THE PROJECT CREATIVE?

1. Ancient Lake Paleohydrology Integration: Connects route planning to Jezero's fundamental science story: "Under a lake at -2,395m, 77% of this route would be underwater."

2. 1-Click Mission Briefing: Solves hackathon judge fatigue by delivering a full, choreographed 38-second demonstration with cinematic stage captions.

3. Live Mobile QR Code: The Mission Dossier features an instant QR code allowing evaluators to scan and inspect the route on their phones.

4. Physical Martian Realism: Incorporates Martian surface gravity (3.72 m/s² / 38% of Earth) and calculates a Local Mean Solar Time (LMST) sunset deadline (17:45 LMST cutoff) to ensure crew return before night temperatures plunge to -85°C.

FACTORS CONSIDERED:

- Planetary Geodesy & Datum: Accurately aligned to Mars Equator and prime meridian coordinates with datum elevation standards.

- Low-Gravity Traction Physics: Factored reduced normal force into regolith slip penalties.

- Real-Time Usability: Client-side canvas shaders run at 60 FPS, ensuring instantaneous responsiveness across all devices.
